decisions.reason: The chain order and forwarding behavior do not change the existing connector types, signals, pin-order policy, or matching-numbering requirement.
The power-chain decision does not alter the I2C cable length, clock speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor configuration.
The same source message already has a complete MODIFY recording the INA219 position and its total downstream 3.3V current coverage; no additional update or removal is required.
The standalone-power state already covers the complete 3.3V rail and sensor debugging; the normal board-chain description does not change its source, activation condition, rating, or powered scope.
The source identifies existing power-board and sensor-board connectors but does not change the connector inventory, count, destinations, or pin-count characterization.
Placing the INA219 downstream of the Schottky diodes is compatible with the existing OR-ing state and does not change the sources, diode method, or source-selection behavior.
The board-chain power path does not affect the charge-status indicator, connector, resistor, or population requirements.
The source describes 3.3V distribution and monitoring, not the switched 5V boost enable, output rating, or powered loads.
The source does not change the addressable LEDs' 5V supply, switching, or data-level-shifting requirements.
The downstream board-chain topology does not resolve or modify the battery connector's placement, form factor, pin functions, mounting style, or pinout ambiguity.
The clarified power path does not change the requirement for local decoupling capacitors.
The board-chain power-distribution decision does not affect panel controls, connector-based mounting, GPIO assignments, reset wiring, touch inputs, or BOOT/EN capacitance.
